name: FQL
title: FQL (Fauna v10)

type.text: **Every expression is checked before it runs**: FQL is statically typed, and a mismatch rejects the query as invalid_query with the source location and a hint, before evaluation

**Sum types exist**: field types and let-bindings take unions such as `status: "cart" | "processing"`, and the type docs state unions "can be combined to emulate abstract data types found in other functional languages"
**Absence is in the type**: `byId()` returns a Document or a typed NullDoc, `?.` chains, `??` defaults, and `!` asserts non-null at run time, so "may be absent" is written where the compiler sees it
**The check is optional per database and per call**: type checking is a database setting (`typechecked: true`) and a driver option, and with it off the same query fails only when the NullDoc arrives

construction.text: **Values bind, they do not sit**: `let` introduces a typed binding, queries compose as expressions, and the language has no assignment that mutates a binding

**Writes validate against the schema**: field definitions, wildcard constraints, and check constraints are enforced by the database on write, in schemaless, permissive, or strict modes the FSL schema chooses

memory.text: **Allocation is the service's**: documents, indexes, and query state live in the Fauna service, and the query text allocates nothing

error.text: **No handling construct exists in the language**: a failed query returns an error response and aborts the transaction, and FQL defines no try, catch, or handler to route around a failure
**No composable result type**: failures cannot ride a value through an expression — only the NullDoc rides `??` — so every caller reads the error envelope out of band
**The error names its place**: the type checker reports `at *query*:3:4` with a source excerpt and a hint naming the operator to add

concurrency.text: **Transactions are the service's**: queries run in strictly serialized transactions across regions, and the language names no threads or tasks

platform.text: **One service spoke FQL**: queries ran only against the Fauna service over its HTTPS API, and the service shut down on 2025-05-30, so the deployment unit was a vendor account that no longer exists
**A poor fit outside operational documents**: the unit is the document, reads ride Fauna indexes, and analytics, reporting, and bulk export move to the snapshot exports the migration guide prescribes

performance.text: **The read rides an index**: collection reads answer from Fauna indexes, and the docs describe index-driven sets as the query's answer shape
**Pricing follows the ops**: the serverless model bills reads, writes, and compute per operation, so a query's cost is a function of the index plan, visible only through the dashboard's query stats

ecosystem.text: **The ecosystem closed with the service**: drivers for JavaScript, Python, Go, C#, and Java remain open source, but the database they talk to shut down, and the promised open-source core engine has no released implementation
**The engine was proprietary**: the service, its storage, and the query engine were never published under an open license — only the drivers and the CLI were — so no second implementation could exist

evolution.text: **The language was replaced once already**: FQL v10 replaced the v4 language wholesale, with a migration guide rather than a compatibility path, before the service itself ended
**The platform is discontinued**: the Fauna service shut down on 2025-05-30, accounts and data were deleted on that date, and the end-of-life FAQ states no extensions were offered

domain.text: **Adopting FQL meant adopting Fauna**: collections, indexes, keys, roles, and user-defined functions are Fauna resources, and the language's Set and document model has no meaning outside the service

**The schema-first model dictates the data architecture**: FSL defines collections, fields, check constraints, and computed fields as deployable source, and the docs frame the database as a deployment target of the schema

learning.text: **A SQL reader meets a functional language**: Sets, higher-order functions, projection syntax, NullDoc handling, and FSL schema deployment have no SQL analog, and the learning path starts at the type system
**Three surfaces at once**: FQL queries, the FSL schema language, and the dashboard shell all carry the data model, and the v10/v4 split adds a second dialect to every search result

syntax.text: **The common query reads like TypeScript**: `Product.byId(id)?.update(data)` states the whole update, and the `?.`, `??`, and `!` operators arrive with widely known meanings

testing.text: **No standard test harness exists in the language**: the docs publish no query-test framework, and a team tests FQL through its host-language test suite against a live database
**No query-plan tool is published**: the dashboard shows per-query stats, and the docs publish no EXPLAIN or plan surface that states how a query will read

security.text: **Queries compose with bound values**: the query is a program, not a concatenated string, values arrive as arguments, and the docs prescribe attribute-based access control through roles rather than string hygiene

reproducibility.text: **A query is request text**: the same FQL on the same schema and data reproduces the same result, and nothing is built

**The executing version is the service's**: the repository names no language or engine version — a `schema_version` comes back in responses — and the one executor that defined semantics no longer runs

supplychain.text: **Drivers carry no signed provenance**: the client libraries publish to npm, PyPI, and the other registries under ordinary package terms, and a consumer trusts what the registry serves

observability.text: **No tracing or metrics standard is part of the language**: monitoring was the dashboard's and the status page's, and the query text carries no trace hook
**No structured logging in the language**: the service kept its own logs, and FQL defines no logging construct a query could call

feedback.text: **No debugger exists**: diagnosis went through the dashboard's query logs and stats and the error envelope
**No maintained editor analysis**: the dashboard shell ran queries with a schema view, and the docs publish no code-assistance surface for FQL in an editor

interop.text: **No foreign-function interface exists**: FQL defines no way to call another language's library in process — not a script embedding, not a native path — so every capability must be an FQL or FSL construct
**No portable target**: a query runs on the Fauna service, and nothing in the language runs without it

governance.text: **Governance was one company**: Fauna, Inc. decided the language's direction, the service's terms, and its end — and no independent body could change any of it
**No public specification exists**: the reference documents the implemented behavior, and no document a second implementation could follow was ever published
**Correctness was what the service did**: no conformance suite or independent implementation ever checked the semantics, so a program's meaning was a property of one closed engine
**The parser was never readable**: the server and its query engine stayed closed source, so the syntax's ground truth lived in a binary the ecosystem could not inspect

tradeoffs: **A type system above a document store**: static typing, unions, and NullDoc handling caught null and shape errors before evaluation — a guarantee no other assessed query DSL offers — and the price was a functional language no SQL reader already knew

**The platform, not the language, ended**: FQL v10's design survives in documentation and open drivers, but the only engine that executed it shut down on 2025-05-30, and the promised open-source core has no release

**Schema as deployed code**: FSL made collections, constraints, and functions source with versioned deploys, and the price was that the database's shape lived in the vendor's service rather than in any file a team owns

**A clean surface with no escape hatches**: no injection surface, no logging, no debugging, no FFI — every operational concern outside the query itself had to route through the vendor's dashboard, API, or support
verdict: FQL v10 was a TypeScript-inspired functional query language over a document-relational store, and the only one of the assessed query DSLs whose expressions are statically checked against a schema with unions, typed NullDocs, and explicit null operators before a query runs. Its costs were the platform's: one proprietary service defined, executed, priced, and then discontinued the language — the service shut down on 2025-05-30, accounts and data were deleted, no specification or conformance mechanism ever existed, and the engine's parser never published. Main strengths: static typing with `?.`/`??`/`!` null handling, FSL schema-as-code with enforced field definitions and check constraints, composable queries with no injection surface, and concise TypeScript-familiar syntax. Main weaknesses: a functional model with a real learning curve, no in-language error handling or result type, no debugging or query-plan tooling, single-vendor governance of a now-defunct proprietary engine, and a lifecycle that ended with the vendor's funding rather than with any technical failure.

energy.text: The engine's energy was the vendor's bill and then the vendor's shutdown; a reader choosing constructs today is reading a language nothing executes, and the levers the syntax exposes — index choice, projection shape — were priced per operation.

ai-readiness.text: A typed functional query language is unusually checkable ground for generated queries — the type checker rejects a generated null dereference before evaluation — but the platform's end means the check ran nowhere for the language's last year, and no model was trained on more than a sliver of v10 code.

safety.text: No certified path; serialized transactions and attribute-based access control were the service's guarantees, stated in its own documentation and ended with the service.

use:data.observation: documents, indexes, and query state live in the Fauna service

use:query.observation: queries ran only against the Fauna service over its HTTPS API

delivery.target: FQL query text and stored FSL/UDF source
delivery.note: queries travel as request text over the service's HTTPS API, and collections, functions, and schema definitions are stored by the database as source; no compiled unit crosses a producer boundary
